evidence.observation: The dependency path is checkout-web -> payment-api -> auth-gateway; AUTH-2026-0318 changed auth-gateway at 14:05Z.

At 14:10Z checkout-web had an 18.7% HTTP 401 rate and 2400 ms p95, payment-api had a 21.2% HTTP 401 rate, and auth-gateway had a 28.4% HTTP 401 rate with notes citing invalid issuer and issuer mismatch.
After deployment of AUTH-2026-0318, auth-gateway used partner-v2 but allowed only partner-v1; validation failed with issuer_not_allowed.
Payment token validation failed upstream at auth-gateway with issuer_not_allowed, and the payment request was rejected as invalid_issuer.
Checkout submit_order failed with 401 from payment-api, and the checkout session was reported auth_failed due to invalid issuer.

excluded_red_herrings.why_not_primary: The database reported normal 35 ms query latency and zero errors; no failing checkout transaction reached it before the auth gate.
The metric notes limit the issue to images, while checkout static assets served normally after retry; this does not explain payment authorization 401s.
These are downstream symptoms consistent with rejected authentication, not an initiating dependency failure.

recommended_next_steps: Immediately restore partner-v2 in auth-gateway allowed_issuers or revert AUTH-2026-0318, following the rollback candidate in the auth log.
Verify JWKS cache namespace and issuer configuration agree across all auth-gateway instances, then retry token validation with a partner-v2 token.
Confirm auth-gateway issuer_not_allowed and HTTP 401 rates return to baseline, then verify payment-api create_payment and checkout-web submit_order succeed.
After recovery, review the change rollout and add a compatibility check for issuer and allowed_issuers before deployment.
